text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain in the leg, particularly when standing for long periods or at the end of the day? Also, is there any foul-smelling discharge coming from the wound?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of DVT and chronic swelling, I suspect venous insufficiency, so REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial Index and REQUEST IMAGES: Lower leg wound photos. Does the wound appear weepy with yellow slough, or is it dry with a pale base?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Blood Pressure 126/84 mmHg, Heart Rate 62/min. Leg Examination: Large ulcer on the right lower leg with varicose veins; bilateral edema (more pronounced on the right); diminished dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on the right; discolored skin with chronic pigmentation. Doppler Ultrasound: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg. Complete Blood Count: WBC, Hemoglobin, and Platelets within normal limits. Wound Culture: No growth of pathogenic bacteria. Note: Ankle-Brachial Index and Lower leg wound photos were requested but results are not currently available in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the Doppler findings of venous reflux and obstruction alongside your history of DVT, I have sufficient evidence to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Ulcer.
